svg.title: AgriASIC Digital Design - Requirements and Scope
svg.desc: Slide 2: functional requirements, constraints, and in-scope boundaries.
svg.text: Requirements and Scope Freeze
Functional Requirements
R1. Autonomous measurement run after start command
R2. Bipolar excitation control with programmable settle time
R3. SAR conversion trigger/control with programmable latency
R4. Paired-sample accumulation: (D+ - D-) / 2 over M pairs
R5. SPI mode-0 control plane with deterministic 2-byte framing
R6. Sticky protocol error observability through STATUS bits
R7. Reset-safe behavior across all digital blocks
R8. Phase-locked FSM plus RV32I + ROM policy control over the inner loop
Timing/Area/Schedule Constraints
C1. 11-week trial GDS target, hard Week-4 feature gate
C2. 8-bit SAR path, fixed-gain TIA assumption for first silicon
C3. Memory/compiler availability resolved in Week 1
C4. Keep a protected FSM-only timing baseline in the descope ladder
C5. SPI/status protocol must support debug and field triage
C6. Keep the programming layer thin; do not place hard timing in firmware
Scope Boundaries
In Scope (Rev 4.1)
- Measurement FSM and configurable timing controls
- Excitation control + polarity/settle handshake
- SAR controller + conversion complete capture
- SPI slave + register map + ACK/NACK/error bytes
- Status/result mirroring and smoke-level self-check TB
- Phase-locked measurement FSM with free-running excitation and RV32I policy layer
Out of Scope (First Implementation)
- On-die excitation amplitude DAC
- Multi-channel sensor muxing and autoranging
- ADC resolution increase beyond 8-bit baseline
- Large debug fabric not tied to closure risk reduction
- General-purpose software stack, OS, or MMU support
Design Rule for Scope Changes
Accept change only if contract, RTL, model, and tests update together.
After Week-4 gate, changes are fix-only unless blocking tapeout risk.
